explanation: In C++, exception handling provides a mechanism to respond to runtime errors, allowing programs to handle unexpected conditions gracefully. The std::out_of_range exception specifically signals that an operation has attempted to access an element outside the valid range, such as an invalid index in a container. Using exceptions like std::out_of_range enables robust error detection and handling, especially when working with standard library containers like std::vector or std::string, which can throw this exception when bounds are exceeded.
